chunks.arabic_text: عَلِيّ بْن مُحَمَّد بْن جَعْفَر بْن عِنْبَسَةَ، الْحَدَّادُ، أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْعَسْكَرِيُّ. ضَعِيفٌ. رَوَى عَنِ الضُّعَفَاءِ. لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ.

translations.en: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn 'Anbasa, al-Haddad (the ironsmith), Abu al-Hasan al-'Askari. Weak. He narrated from the weak narrators. He is not turned to.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Ali ibn Muhammad as a weak narrator whose reliability is compromised by his transmission from other weak sources, leading scholars to disregard his narrations. The epithet 'al-Haddad' (the ironsmith) highlights his trade, while 'al-'Askari' links him to the Samarra region, providing geographical and social context to his status in the science of narrator criticism (*ilm al-rijal*).
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn Muhammad al-Haddad and what is his status in hadith sciences?

key_terms.لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ: He is not turned to / not relied upon
